questoes.pergunta: For the model, what is the main role of a tool's `description` field?
opcoes: Documentation for the developers who maintain the tool; the model uses only the `name`
It's the criterion the model uses to decide whether and when to call that tool
It serves only to validate the arguments before execution
It's optional when the `input_schema` already has well-named `properties`
questoes.explicacao: The model reads the description when choosing a tool: purpose, when to use it, input, output, edge cases, and how it differs from its neighbors.
feedbacks: Tempting because in code a 'description' is usually a comment; but the model reads the description to decide.
Correct: the description is the selection criterion, not decoration.
Argument validation is done by the schema (and `strict`), not by the description.
Property names help, but they don't say when to use the tool or how it differs from the others.

questoes.pergunta: What requirement does `strict: true` impose on a tool's `input_schema`, and what is the recommendation for fields that may be missing?
opcoes: Every property must have an `enum` listing its possible values
The schema must use `oneOf` for each possible type of each property
Only that the `name` follow snake_case
`additionalProperties: false` on every object; optional properties are allowed (they count toward a limit), but the recommendation is `required` + nullable
questoes.explicacao: Strict requires `additionalProperties: false` on every object. Optional properties are allowed but count toward a total per-request limit [volatile]; in practice, prefer putting everything in `required`, with a nullable type for whatever may be missing. It also accepts only a subset of JSON Schema.
feedbacks: Enum is advisable, but strict doesn't require it.
`oneOf` isn't a requirement (and it isn't even among the constructs documented as supported; `anyOf` has limitations).
Naming conventions have nothing to do with strict.
Correct: a closed object is the requirement; `required` + nullable is the practical recommendation.

questoes.pergunta: An agent confuses `get_customer` and `lookup_client`, whose descriptions are nearly identical. What is the first recommended fix?
opcoes: Rewrite the descriptions to separate the purposes (or merge the two tools)
Train a classifier that picks the tool before the model receives the question
Switch to a larger model
Force `tool_choice` to the most-used tool
questoes.explicacao: Overlapping tools cause misrouting; the simplest fix is to separate the purposes in the description/name, or to merge them.
feedbacks: Correct: tackling the ambiguity at the interface is the simplest fix that works.
More complex than necessary; the ambiguity remains in the definition.
A larger model still reads two identical descriptions.
Forcing one tool breaks the cases where the other one is right.

questoes.pergunta: The order lookup tool ran normally and found no orders for the customer. How should the result come back?
opcoes: `is_error: true` with a transient category
`is_error: true` with a validation category
Success with an empty result (e.g., an empty list or `found=false`)
Don't return a `tool_result`, so the model notices the emptiness and tries another tool
questoes.explicacao: Empty ≠ failure: the lookup ran, and 'nothing found' is valid information.
feedbacks: Transient is when the lookup did NOT run (timeout, 503).
The input was valid; there's nothing to correct.
Correct: an empty result is a success.
Every `tool_use` needs a matching `tool_result`.

questoes.pergunta: An error saying 'above the refund limit allowed by the policy' should be classified as:
opcoes: Transient, retryable with backoff
Business, not retryable: explain the policy or escalate
Validation: fix the amount's format and try again
Permission: renew the token and try again
questoes.explicacao: A policy violation is a business error: trying again will never succeed.
feedbacks: Waiting doesn't change the policy; retrying here is wasteful.
Correct.
The format was correct; the problem is the business rule.
It's not a missing credential; it's a policy limit.

questoes.pergunta: The search backend went down and the tool returned `[]` as if it were a success. Which anti-pattern is this?
opcoes: Silent error suppression
Generic error
Overlapping tool
Too many tools on the same agent, confusing selection
questoes.explicacao: Returning empty when the search didn't run hides the failure: the model concludes something false ('it doesn't exist').
feedbacks: Correct.
A generic error is 'Operation failed'; here no error is even signaled.
It has nothing to do with two similar tools.
It has nothing to do with the number of tools.

questoes.pergunta: What is the guideline for the number of tools visible to an agent at decision time?
opcoes: Up to 50, as long as the descriptions are good
Exactly one, to avoid ambiguity
As many as fit in the context window
About 4–5
questoes.explicacao: 4–5 tools per agent; with many more than that, selection degrades, and the fix is to distribute them across specialized subagents (or use tool search).
feedbacks: Good descriptions don't make up for volume.
One tool per agent creates coordination overhead with no gain.
Fitting in the window doesn't mean selecting well.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: When is tool search with `defer_loading` appropriate?
opcoes: Whenever more than one tool is declared, to save tokens on any request
Only when the model doesn't support `tool_choice`
With a large catalog: 10+ tools, >10k tokens of definitions, or several MCP servers
When you want to prevent the model from calling tools without removing them from the request
questoes.explicacao: Tool search loads definitions on demand when the catalog is large; keep 3–5 frequently used tools non-deferred.
feedbacks: With few tools, the search overhead isn't worth it.
It has nothing to do with `tool_choice`.
Correct.
To prevent calls, you use `tool_choice: none`.

questoes.pergunta: Which `tool_choice` makes the model respond only in text while keeping the tools declared in the request?
opcoes: `{"type": "none"}`
`{"type": "auto"}`
`{"type": "any"}`
Remove the `tools` array
questoes.explicacao: `none` = text only; the tools remain declared (and the cache prefix doesn't change).
feedbacks: Correct.
`auto` lets the model decide, so it may call tools.
`any` forces it to call some tool.
Removing `tools` changes the prefix and invalidates the cache; it's not the same as `none`.

opcoes: Turns off tool use in the request
Limits it to at most one tool call per response
Makes the client execute the tools sequentially, but the model still emits several
Forces the model to call exactly two tools
questoes.explicacao: It limits the model to one call per response (with `any`/`tool`, exactly one).
feedbacks: To turn off tools, you use `none`.
Correct.
The restriction is on what the model emits, not on how the client executes.
No such behavior exists.

questoes.pergunta: [volatile] On newer models, a forced `tool_choice` of `any` or `tool` returns a 400. If the goal was just to get JSON in the right format, what is the alternative?
opcoes: Use an assistant prefill with `{`
Repeat the request until it no longer returns a 400
Structured outputs (`output_config.format` with `json_schema`)
Use `tool_choice: none` and ask in the prompt for the response to be valid JSON
questoes.explicacao: Structured outputs solve 'always JSON matching the schema'; another option is `auto` + an instruction naming the tool + `strict`.
feedbacks: Prefill also returns a 400 on newer models.
A 400 is an invalid-request error; repeating it doesn't help.
Correct.
Asking for JSON in prose doesn't guarantee the format.

questoes.pergunta: How are Anthropic-defined tools (e.g., web search) declared?
opcoes: With complete `name`, `description`, and `input_schema`
Only via an MCP server
With `strict: true` required
By `type` + `name`, without `input_schema`
questoes.explicacao: Anthropic-defined tools use a versioned `type` + `name`; the model already knows the schema.
feedbacks: That's the format for a custom client-side tool.
They don't depend on MCP.
Strict is for custom tools.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: A server-side web search tool failed. How does this show up for your code?
opcoes: HTTP 200, with an error object inside the result block
HTTP 500 with the tool's error message in the response body
Always HTTP 429
The response comes back empty, with no `content`
questoes.explicacao: Server-side tool errors come with HTTP 200 and the error inside the result (e.g., `max_uses_exceeded`). Checking only the HTTP status won't catch them.
feedbacks: Correct.
Tempting because that's how APIs usually fail, but that's not the case here.
Rate limiting is something else and isn't the tool's error mechanism.
The response comes back normally, with the error inside the block.

questoes.pergunta: The model emitted three `tool_use` blocks in one response and one of them failed. How should you return them?
opcoes: Three separate `user` messages, one per result, in the order each tool finished
One `user` message with only the two that succeeded
One `user` message with all three `tool_result` blocks; the failed one with `is_error: true`
Resend the request without the tool that failed, so the model doesn't keep trying it
questoes.explicacao: All `tool_result` blocks go in a single `user` message, each with its `tool_use_id`, including the one that failed.
feedbacks: Splitting into several messages breaks the return pattern.
Every `tool_use` needs its `tool_result`.
Correct.
Changing the tools invalidates the cache and hides the failure from the model.

questoes.pergunta: The response came back with `stop_reason: "pause_turn"`. What should you do?
opcoes: Treat it as the end and show the text to the user
Resend the conversation with this assistant response so the model can continue
Increase `max_tokens` and repeat the request from scratch, since the response was cut off
Escalate to a human
questoes.explicacao: `pause_turn` = the server-side loop hit its iteration cap; the response is partial and must be sent back to continue.
feedbacks: The response is partial; treating it as the end delivers an incomplete result.
Correct.
That would be the response to `max_tokens`, not to `pause_turn`.
Nothing here requires a human; it's a technical continuation.
